Why Index Choice Matters for Graph Queries

By Jane Example

This is the first paragraph of a fictional article written for testing. It explains that the way data is indexed changes how quickly a multi-hop query can walk from one record to the next.

The second paragraph describes a toy benchmark. In this made-up example, a query that follows three relationships finishes faster when adjacency is stored next to each node.

The third paragraph adds a caveat. The toy benchmark used a small dataset that fit in memory, so the result may not hold when the working set is larger than available RAM.

The fourth paragraph compares the approach with a relational join. Joins can be competitive when the query touches only one or two relationships and the right indexes exist.

The fifth paragraph concludes that teams should measure their own workloads before choosing, because synthetic examples like this one rarely match production traffic.
